subject: food-technology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which type of fat is generally considered the least healthy and is linked to raised blood cholesterol?
questions.explain: Saturated fat, found mainly in animal products, can raise blood cholesterol and increase the risk of heart disease.

questions.q: Which nutrient is the body's main and preferred source of energy?
questions.explain: Carbohydrates are the body's primary energy source, providing glucose for cells.

questions.q: The deficiency disease rickets in children is caused mainly by a lack of:
questions.explain: Rickets results from a lack of vitamin D and calcium, leading to soft, weak and bowed bones.

questions.q: According to the Eatwell Guide, which group should make up the largest proportion of the diet alongside fruit and vegetables?
options: Beans, pulses, fish, eggs and meat
questions.explain: The Eatwell Guide shows fruit, vegetables and starchy carbohydrates forming the largest parts of a balanced diet.

questions.q: Which vitamin is made by the skin in sunlight and helps the body absorb calcium?
questions.explain: Vitamin D is produced in the skin from sunlight and is needed to absorb calcium for healthy bones.

questions.q: Dietary fibre (NSP) is important mainly because it:
options: Helps prevent constipation and keeps the digestive system healthy
questions.explain: Fibre adds bulk to faeces, aids digestion and helps prevent constipation and bowel problems.

questions.q: Which mineral is most important for building strong bones and teeth?
questions.explain: Calcium is essential for the formation and maintenance of strong bones and teeth.

questions.q: Which condition is most strongly linked to a long-term diet high in saturated fat and salt?
questions.explain: A diet high in saturated fat and salt raises the risk of coronary heart disease.

questions.q: A protein that contains all the essential amino acids the body needs is described as having:
questions.explain: High biological value (HBV) proteins, such as those from meat, fish, eggs and soya, contain all the essential amino acids.

questions.q: Combining two low biological value plant proteins to provide all essential amino acids is called:
questions.explain: Complementary proteins, such as beans on toast, combine different LBV proteins so all essential amino acids are supplied.

questions.q: A diet deficient in iron over time is most likely to cause:
questions.explain: Iron is needed to make haemoglobin, so a lack of iron causes iron-deficiency anaemia.

questions.q: Vitamin C is needed mainly for which of the following?
options: Healthy gums, wound healing and iron absorption
questions.explain: Vitamin C maintains healthy connective tissue, aids wound healing and helps the body absorb iron.
